messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: High-rate Prefill OOMs detected in cluster gpu-pool-7. 23 container restarts in 5m, automated mitigation triggered: reduced scheduling. Pager: @elena. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom
elena (oncall): taking this. joining bridge now. can someone paste the first failing stack?
chris (eng-runtime): attaching short log. reproducible on long prompt workloads (user streams with ~6k context). kernel shows CUDA OOM during prefill.
chris (eng-runtime): ```
E 23:10:12 model_infer.cpp:421 Prefill: allocate KV cache 1.8G failed: CUDA out of memory
E 23:10:12 container manager: restart container: id=abcd1234 node=node-172 reason=OOM
```
elena (oncall): thanks. are noisy tenants involved? any single customer spiking?
chris (eng-runtime): yes — traffic map shows heavy tail from cust:acme-streaming (20% of prefill tokens in window). Also seeing multi-tenant KV growth causing fragmentation (kvcache-trim not reclaiming fast enough).
chris (eng-runtime): preliminary root-cause: long prefill sequences + kvcache fragmentation + model variant with large kv state. fallback model small-quantized has ~40% lower KV live memory.
elena (oncall): immediate mitigation suggestion?
chris (eng-runtime): 1) apply temporary streaming token throttle for cust:acme-streaming (rate-limit prefill tokens) 2) enable cold-model fallback for that customer (route to openllama-7b-q4) 3) trigger kvcache-trim on nodes node-170..173 4) avoid rolling restarts unless needed
elena (oncall): implement 1 & 2 now. sam, can you take kvcache trims and watch for restarts?
sam (eng-oncall): on it — running trimming job across gpu-pool-7 now. will tail logs.
chris (eng-runtime): config to throttle (example):
```json
{"route":"/v1/streams","customer":"cust:acme-streaming","prefill_max_tokens":1024}
```
chris (eng-runtime): CS message draft for Mike below. please sanity-check.
mike (customer-success): paste it here. I can send once approved.
chris (eng-runtime): "We observed elevated container restarts affecting streaming sessions for customers with very long prompts. We've applied a temporary throttling and routed affected sessions to a smaller fallback model to stabilize latency while we complete remediation. No data was exposed; we are monitoring and will follow up with timeline and mitigation details."
mike (customer-success): looks good — add expected ETA for rollback? suggest "we expect stabilization in ~30-45m"
elena (oncall): agree. add point about engineering working on durable fix (kvcache trimming + model variant autoswap improvements).
nora (support): flagging internal incident tag and customer list in CRM for outreach. I'll queue messages for top 3 affected accounts.
sam (eng-oncall): trimming complete on node-170..173, memory reclaimed ~2.1GB each. tail shows no further immediate restarts.
elena (oncall): nice. lifting some scheduling constraints but keep throttle in place for cust:acme-streaming until we confirm 30m stability.
chris (eng-runtime): will open a follow-up issue to add: better kvcache compaction, earlier cold-model swap heuristic, and telemetry for prefill-kv growth.
elena (oncall): handing off to @sam for next rotation. Sam, you're on-call for the next 2h to monitor. I'll update incident channel with customer-facing note.
sam (eng-oncall): taking over. monitoring grafana alerts and restarting bridge checks. ping me if restarts resume. :thumbsup:
mike (customer-success): sent customer notes to affected accounts, included ETA ~45m and workaround. no escalation requests yet.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Automated mitigation record: throttle applied to cust:acme-streaming, fallback routing enabled, kvcache-trim job completed. Incident state: mitigation in-progress.
elena (oncall): closing pager for now — move to incident-review label and create postmortem if restarts reoccur. good job team :clap:"
